name: Circadian pathway: ipRGC to SCN to pineal melatonin
function: Photic entrainment of the master circadian clock and downstream control of pineal melatonin secretion

steps.cellBodies: Intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells (ipRGCs), melanopsin-containing

decussation.where: a substantial component of the retinohypothalamic tract crosses in the optic chiasm to innervate both suprachiasmatic nuclei

steps.neurotransmitter: glutamate (retinal ganglion cell output; not explicitly stated for this exact step)

evidence.quote: Intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells (ipRGCs) containing the blue light-sensitive photopigment melanopsin transmit light signals via the retinohypothalamic tract directly to the SCN, synchronizing SCN neurons to the external light-dark cycle.
During the daytime, light stimulates the retinohypothalamic pineal pathway. The retinal ganglion cells activate the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) through the optic nerve.
These endogenous SCH rhythms are adjusted daily (entrained) to the environmental light/ dark cycle through a direct projection from the retina to the SCH
In rodents [338] as well as humans [82], this tract terminates in the ventral part of the SCH.

Specialized ganglia take the impulses generated by the light to the suprachiasmatic nucleus of the hypothalamus. The fibers from the hypothalamus then give off to the superior cervical ganglia in the spinal cord.

The rostroventral part of the paraventricular nucleus (PVH) receives a direct projection from the SCH which is augmented by indirect projections via the subparaventricular zone (SPZ) and dorsomedial hypothalamus nucleus (DMH).

steps.terminatesIn: intermediolateral cell column of the upper thoracic spinal cord

evidence.quote: The first-order neurons originate in the hypothalamus and descend uncrossed through the midbrain and pons, terminating in the intermediolateral cell columns at the C8 through T2 levels of the spinal cord, known as the ciliospinal center of Budge.
Many neurons in the PVH and DMH have long, descending axons that pass to autonomic centres in the brain stem and spinal cord
The projection to the pineal includes sympathetic preganglionic neurons in the rostral part of the spinal intermediolateral cell column and postganglionic neurons in the superior cervical ganglion.

steps.cellBodies: Intermediolateral cell column preganglionic sympathetic neurons
courseVia: preganglionic sympathetic fibres via the sympathetic chain

evidence.quote: Second-order preganglionic neurons exit the spinal cord at the T1 level and enter the cervical sympathetic chain, where they ascend to synapse in the superior cervical ganglion at the C3 through C4 levels.
The projection to the pineal includes sympathetic preganglionic neurons in the rostral part of the spinal intermediolateral cell column and postganglionic neurons in the superior cervical ganglion.
From the spinal cord, signals are relayed back to the pineal gland via postganglionic neurons.
The sympathetic innervation is from the superior cervical ganglion, while the parasympathetic innervation is from the optic and pterygopalatine ganglia.
These fibres form part of the projections by which the SCH controls secretion of melatonin from the pineal gland

unsourced.text: At night, reduced SCN inhibition of the sympathetic pathway is generally described as disinhibiting norepinephrine release onto pinealocytes to drive melatonin synthesis; the specific mechanistic wording in the opened StatPearls chapter (S19) contained an apparent internal inconsistency (referring to melatonin release 'from the pituitary' in one sentence, though the chapter's own title and other sentences correctly identify the pineal gland as the source), so that specific sentence was not quoted verbatim for this fact.
Melatonin synthesis from serotonin via AANAT (arylalkylamine N-acetyltransferase) and HIOMT/ASMT enzymes was not found described with a quotable, openable source in this session.

Melatonin synthesis from serotonin via AANAT (arylalkylamine N-acetyltransferase) and HIOMT/ASMT enzymes was not found described anywhere in the opened Nieuwenhuys hypothalamus chapter (ch10); the chapter describes the neural circuitry controlling pineal secretion but not the pinealocyte's intracellular biosynthetic pathway.

The precise routing of the retinohypothalamic tract's decussating component through the optic chiasm to reach the contralateral SCN was not found stated in these exact terms in the opened text; S1 states only that the tract terminates in the ventral SCN in both rodents and humans, without describing the chiasmal crossing explicitly.
